newsitem.title: USA: Plenty of Baptists at Disney World after boycott.
newsitem.headline: Plenty of Baptists at Disney World after boycott.

text.p: It was not hard to find Southern Baptists at Walt Disney World on the first weekend after their leaders urged members to boycott Walt Disney Co fare.
"We already had our tickets and reservations," said Mitch Johnson, a 33-year-old father of three from South Carolina. "I dont know if we'll come back. We'll have to see what they say at church."
Said Tracy Martinez of Coral Gables, Florida: "Oh, I don't think we're supposed to boycott Disney World. It's just the bad movies and stuff. But I think they should definitely keep the gays out."

In Dallas last week, 12,000 delegates at the Southern Baptist Convention's annual meeting voted overwhelmingly for a non-binding boycott against Disney and its subsidiaries by their 15.7 million members. The vote was sparked by corporate policies the conservative Christians say are too tolerant of homosexuals.

These policies include extending employee benefits to gay and lesbian partners and the annual Gay Days events at Walt Disney World. The park does not sponsor Gay Days, but it also does nothing to discourage the profitable influx of gay and lesbian tourists during the first weekend of June.

While Disney's ABC network of broadcast and cable stations is available to most Americans at home, its sprawling theme parks, retail outlets and other attractions are practically a mainstay for millions of vacationers each year.
"This could be our last trip for awhile. We'll have to see what steps Disney is willing to take," said Rusty Anderson of Birmingham, Alabama.
What about watching college football on Disney-owned cable station ESPN?
"Well, I don't see what football has to do with anything," Anderson said.
College football is part of the boycott if it is shown on ESPN. And it is not only movies such as Pulp Fiction that Baptist leaders want to boycott -- Snow White is on the list, too.
But not all Baptists support the boycott.
"I'm not going to boycott," Kay Sanders of Daytona Beach, Florida, a mother of four, said. "It's crazy. Kids have to be someplace, and there aren't many places safer than Disney World.
"And if they don't watch Disney movies, what are they supposed to watch. You can't just keep them in church all the time," she added.
In the Orlando area, most Baptist ministers have said they will not urge their congregations to boycott. Their congregations, totaling about 70,000 members, often include Disney employees.
